Golden Leek & Pear
Skillet
PREP
COOK
YIELD
12 min 18 min Serves 2
Ingredients
2 small leeks, sliced
1 firm pear, diced
1 ½ tbsp olive oil
¾ cup / 180 ml oat cream
½ tsp crushed tennel seed
Salt, to taste
Method
1. Warm the oil in a skillet. Add the leeks
and stir until soft.
2. Fold in the pear and fennel seed. Pour in
the oat cream and simmer until the pear
is tender.
3. Season with salt and spoon into shallow
bowls.

changes are half the fun!

Smoky Millet à la
Brume
Ingredients
¾ cup millet, rinsed
1 ½ cups vegetable stock
1 red pepper, chopped
2 tsp sunflower oil
½ tsp smoked paprika
1 tbsp lemon juice
Method
Toast the millet in a dry pot until fragrant.
Add the stock and cover. In a skillet,
soften the pepper in the oil, then stir in the
paprika. When the millet has absorbed the
stock, fluff it with a fork and fold in the
pepper and lemon juice.

Nocturne Mushroom Börek
PREP
COOK
25 minutes
30 minutes
YIELD
Makes 6 coils
Ingredients
Filling
250 g chestnut mushrooms, chopped
1 small onion, minced
1 tbsp olive oil
⅓ cup crumbled white cheese
Assembly
6 sheets filo pastry
3 tbsp melted butter
1 tsp nigella seeds
Method
1. Heat the oil and soften the onion. Add the mushrooms and cook until their moisture has evaporated. Cool,
then stir in the cheese.
2. Brush each filo sheet with butter. Add a strip of filling, roll into a loose coil and place on a tray.
3. Brush the coils with the remaining butter, scatter over the seeds and bake at 190°C until crisp and golden.

Salad

2 cups sorrel leaves

Charred Carrot Nests
OTAL
35 min
PREP
YIELD
15 min 20 min Serves 3
Ingredients
400 g carrots, shaved into ribbons
1 tbsp sesame oil
2 tsp soy sauce
1 tbsp rice vinegar
½ tsp brown sugar
2 tbsp toasted pumpkin seeds
Method
1. Toss the carrot ribbons with the sesame oil and spread loosely on a hot tray.
2. Roast at 220°C until the edges darken. Whisk the soy sauce, vinegar and sugar together.

Saffron Quince Pilaf
Contributed by Elvi Rook • Edited by the kitchen circle
TOTAL
YIELD
50 minutes Serves 4-5
Ingredients
For the rice
250 g long-grain rice
500 ml vegetable stock
A pinch of saffron
½ tsp fine salt
For the quince
1 quince, peeled and diced
2 tbsp unsalted butter
1 tbsp honey
⅓ cup chopped pistachios
At the stove
1. Rinse the rice. Put it in a pot with the stock, saffron and salt, then cover and simmer until the
liquid is absorbed.
2. Melt the butter in a skillet. Add the quince and cook gently until tender, then glaze with the
honey.
3. Fluff the rice, fold through the quince and scatter with pistachios.

Celeriac Rain Soup
PREP
COOK
YIELD
15 minutes 25 minutes Serves 4
500 g celeriac, peeled and cubed
1 leek, sliced
1 tbsp olive oil
750 ml vegetable stock
½ cup / 120 ml cream
¼ tsp ground white pepper
Method
Soften the leek in the oil. Add the celeriac and stock, cover and simmer until the celeriac
crushes easily. Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and white pepper, and warm through
gently.

Pepper Jam Onigiri

Ingredients
2 cups cooked short-grain rice
2 tbsp red pepper jam
½ tsp rice vinegar
¼ tsp fine salt
2 nori sheets, cut into strips
Directions
1. Mix the warm rice with the vinegar and salt.
2. With damp hands, flatten a small handful of rice.
Put a little pepper jam in the centre and close
the rice around it.
3. Shape into a triangle and wrap the base with a
nori strip. Repeat with the remaining rice and
filling.

Cumin Apple Khichdi
Thread #2468 • 18 replies • 624 views
Posted October 21 • 17:26 1 42
This is my soft, spoonable apple variation. Here's the recipe I settled on.
Omi Thistle
Member
126 posts
Joined April
TOTAL
YIELD
40 min
Serves 2-3
Ingredients
½ cup split yellow mung dal
½ cup short-grain rice
3 cups water
1 small tart apple, diced
1 tbsp ghee
¾ tsp cumin seeds
½ tsp salt
Method
1. Rinse the dal and rice together. Place in a pot with the water and salt, then simmer gently until soft.
2. Heat the ghee in a small pan. Sizzle the cumin seeds, add the apple and soften it.
3. Fold the apple mixture into the rice and dal, loosening with a splash of water if needed.

The Glass Marrow: a bright little supper room
Yara Penn
Dining journal • October 24
***** 4.6 / 5 • Reader score: 4.7 from 218 visits
VISIT NOTES
The Glass Marrow
Fable Quay, lantern district
Carrot ribbon plate R95
Bean purée & bread R110
Plum dessert R80
The Glass Marrow glows at the end of a quiet lane. Our table overlooked a tiny
courtyard, and the staff let us linger over the changing colours of the windows.
The carrot ribbon plate with toasted seeds was the highlight. A pale bean
purée came with crisp bread and herb oil; the plum dessert tasted gently
smoky. We asked how the kitchen made the puree, but the chef kept that
secret.
We waited 25 minutes for a table. The room grew lively, though conversation
stayed easy. I would come back for the courtyard alone.
Our bill: R570 for two, including drinks.
Paid independently. No cooking instructions were
supplied by the kitchen.
